clips.text: You step into the morning sun — and within five minutes, your skin is on fire. About 1 in 100,000 people live like this: allergic to sunlight itself.
The suit goes on before the door opens: visor, gloves, ultraviolet-proof fabric, sunscreen like armour. Miss one patch, and the sun finds it.
The cause is a broken repair crew — eight genes that should fix sun damage in your DNA, switched off. The damage stays, and the risk of skin cancer is about 1,000 times yours.
So these kids live at night. At Camp Sundown, the camp day starts at sunset — baseball at midnight, swimming under the moon, a bonfire at two in the morning.
There is no cure. Only the suit, the shade, and the night. The sun was never the problem. The repair crew was.
You step into the morning sun — and within five minutes, your skin is on fire. Now you know what that freedom is worth.
